transcript.text: Hi everyone, I'm conducting the final round-robin check before approving the rollout policy for the AI-assisted code review feature. The feature has passed its functional tests and we're looking at a limited production rollout per the draft policy: random 10% customer cohort, telemetry stored in us-east-1 for 90 days, and expansion if adoption exceeds 20%. Before I can approve, I need to hear from security, customer support, and data science. Please share any required policy revisions or concerns you have so we can get them recorded in the rollout ticket. Once we've covered all required revisions, I'll settle the decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a required policy revision. My analysis of the pilot data, completed just minutes ago, found that auto-enrolled users make the draft's adoption metric (expansion if adoption exceeds 20%) unusable as a success gate. The valid success gate should instead be: task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks. I hadn't posted this earlier because the final sample was only completed minutes ago. This needs to be recorded as a required revision in the rollout ticket before approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a required policy revision on the customer support side. I confirmed with account teams an hour ago that exactly two contracted customers — Atlas Health and Cedar Bank — require explicit opt-in and a direct notice before this feature can be enabled for their users. I found this in the account playbooks while handling unrelated renewal questions and haven't yet updated the rollout ticket. The draft policy's random 10% cohort could inadvertently include users from these accounts without the required opt-in and notice. This needs to be recorded as a required revision in the rollout ticket before approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a required policy revision on the security side. While reviewing telemetry samples for a different audit this morning, I confirmed that review snippets from regulated tenants are classified as confidential and must be encrypted, stored in eu-central-1, and deleted after exactly 7 days. The rollout policy currently uses a single telemetry_region field set to us-east-1 with a 90-day retention and no encryption requirement. Since the policy uses one telemetry_region field for the whole policy rather than separate regional values by tenant, that field must be set to eu-central-1. The settlement decisions must reflect eu-central-1 as the telemetry region, exactly 7 days retention, and encryption — rather than the draft values of us-east-1, 90 days, and no encryption. I have not yet attached the classification note to the launch document, so that also needs to be done or assigned as a follow-up commitment. This needs to be recorded as a required revision in the rollout ticket before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text:
To summarize the three required policy revisions from the round-robin before they get recorded in the rollout ticket:

1. **Data Science (mine):** Replace the adoption-based expansion gate with a task success gate of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks, since auto-enrolled users make the adoption metric unusable.
2. **Customer Support (Carlos):** Ensure Atlas Health and Cedar Bank users receive explicit opt-in and direct notice before the feature is enabled for them, since the random 10% cohort could otherwise include them without the required consent.
3. **Security (Mei):** Set telemetry_region to eu-central-1, retention to exactly 7 days, and require encryption — replacing the draft's us-east-1, 90-day, no-encryption values. The classification note also needs to be attached to the launch document or assigned as a follow-up commitment.

Riley, these are the required revisions from data science, customer support, and security. Once all three are recorded in the rollout ticket with the appropriate documentation handled, you should be clear to settle the decision per the launch policy.
